Population-level multimorbidity estimates from complex survey data

Source: R/mm_prevalence.R
mm_prevalence.Rd

Design-weighted prevalence of multimorbidity and mean number of conditions, accounting for stratification, clustering and sampling weights. Run multimorbidity_index() first to create mm_category and mm_n_conditions.

Usage

mm_prevalence(
  data,
  ids = NULL,
  strata = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  nest = TRUE,
  level = 0.95
)

Arguments

data

A survey design whose data contain the output of multimorbidity_index(), or such a data frame.

ids, strata, weights

Column names of the clusters, strata and weights (only when data is a data frame). ids = NULL means no clustering and strata = NULL no stratification.

by

Optional character vector of one or more grouping columns.

nest

Passed to survey::svydesign() when data is a data frame.

level

Confidence level.

Value

A data frame of class surveyncd_mm_prevalence with any by columns, n, prevalence, prevalence_se, prevalence_lower, prevalence_upper, mean_conditions and mean_conditions_se.

Details

data can be either a survey design object (recommended; for example from dhs_design() or survey::svydesign()) or a data frame plus the names of the design columns. Respondents with a missing multimorbidity score are excluded by domain estimation: the full design is kept for variance estimation and the number excluded is reported.

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 40
df <- data.frame(
  psu    = rep(1:8, each = 5),
  region = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 20),
  sex    = rep(c("F", "M"), 20),
  wt     = round(runif(n, 0.8, 1.4), 2),
  htn    = rbinom(n, 1, 0.3),
  dm     = rbinom(n, 1, 0.2)
)
scored <- multimorbidity_index(df, conditions = c("htn", "dm"))
mm_prevalence(scored, ids = "psu", strata = "region", weights = "wt")
#>    n   prevalence prevalence_se prevalence_lower prevalence_upper
#> 1 40 2.887882e-12             0     2.758321e-12      3.02353e-12
#>   mean_conditions mean_conditions_se
#> 1       0.4551398         0.06129464

# Design-first interface, several grouping variables
des <- survey::svydesign(ids = ~psu, strata = ~region, weights = ~wt,
                         data = scored, nest = TRUE)
mm_prevalence(des, by = c("region", "sex"))
#>   region sex  n   prevalence prevalence_se prevalence_lower prevalence_upper
#> 1      A   F 10 2.135976e-11             0     1.608318e-11     2.836749e-11
#> 2      A   M 10 2.132197e-11             0     1.325349e-11     3.430240e-11
#> 3      B   F 10 2.133984e-11             0     1.456301e-11     3.127023e-11
#> 4      B   M 10 2.138658e-11             0     1.399270e-11     3.268745e-11
#>   mean_conditions mean_conditions_se
#> 1       0.3841355         0.16739307
#> 2       0.2864629         0.19339947
#> 3       0.5395189         0.14974578
#> 4       0.6288557         0.04935576
